SELECTED_INDEX: 2  
CONFIDENCE: 0.29  
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by two very strong bands at 998 cm⁻¹ and 1028 cm⁻¹, the characteristic pair of ring-breathing / in-plane C–H bending vibrations of a monosubstituted benzene.  A second strong band at 1245 cm⁻¹ fits the intense νas(Ar–O–C) stretch of an aryl-alkyl ether (anisole–type compounds typically give a 1240–1270 cm⁻¹ Raman band).  Additional medium bands at 1116 and 1079 cm⁻¹ match the symmetric C–O–C stretches of an alkyl aryl-ether.  Peaks at 615 cm⁻¹ and 594 cm⁻¹ correspond well to an aliphatic C–Cl stretching vibration, supporting the presence of a chloro-substituted side chain.  The C–H stretching region shows aromatic bands at 3072 cm⁻¹ and aliphatic bands at 2981, 2938 and 2880 cm⁻¹, consistent with an ethoxy substituent (two CH₂ groups, no free OH or NH stretches observed).  

Among the candidates, only molecule 2 (ClCCOc1ccccc1, 2-chloroethoxybenzene) simultaneously provides:  
• a single aryl substituent (needed for the 998/1028 cm⁻¹ doublet),  
• an Ar–O–C ether linkage (1245 & 1116 cm⁻¹), and  
• an aliphatic C–Cl bond (∼600–700 cm⁻¹ band).  

Other candidates either lack the strong Ar–O–C feature (1, 4, 9), possess N–H or O–H groups that should give >3200 cm⁻¹ bands (5, 7, 8, 10), or contain Br instead of Cl (1), which would shift the C–halogen stretch lower (∼500 cm⁻¹).  Therefore candidate 2 provides the most coherent explanation of the observed Raman peaks.
